Some people argue that university education should be provided free of charge to every student, while others believe that students should contribute to the cost. In my opinion, governments should cover tuition fees, because the benefits to society outweigh the expense.

The main argument for free higher education is that it gives every young person the same opportunity. When students from low-income families do not have to worry about tuition fees, they are more likely to choose courses that match their abilities rather than their budgets. Germany is a clear example: since it abolished tuition fees, the number of students from working-class backgrounds has risen steadily.

In addition, a well-educated population supports economic growth. Graduates tend to earn higher salaries and therefore pay more tax, so the money that is spent on universities is partly returned to the state over time. A country that invests in education also becomes more attractive to companies that need skilled workers.

On the other hand, critics point out that free tuition places a heavy burden on public budgets and may lead to overcrowded classes. This concern is valid, but it can be addressed by limiting the number of places in each course rather than by charging fees that exclude poorer students.

In conclusion, although free university education is expensive, I believe it is a worthwhile investment, because it widens access to learning and strengthens the economy in the long term.
